## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Asaññasattupikakathā* (Kv 15.10) is a debate located in the fifteenth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu* within the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. The discussion addresses the proposition *Saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpatti asaññasattupikā ti*, examining whether the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling leads to rebirth in the realm of non-percipient beings (*asaññasatta*) [Dube 1980]. In the *Kathāvatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, the attainment of cessation (*saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpatti*, also glossed as *asaññasamāpatti*) is distinguished into two forms: a mundane (*lokiyā*) attainment practiced by ordinary people (*puthujjana*) that conduces to rebirth in the realm of non-ideation (*asaññasattupikā*), and a supramundane (*lokuttarā*) attainment cultivated by noble ones (*ariya*) that does not (*nāsaññasattupikā*); this Theravāda stance is maintained in opposition to the views of the Hetuvādins [Deleanu 2006; Dube 1980].
